own_solution.law: For longitudinal rod waves, v = sqrt(Y/rho). The fundamental frequency is f = v/(2L), and adjacent dust nodes are separated by d = c/(2f) = cL sqrt(rho/Y). Converting Y = 70000 MPa to 7.00e10 Pa gives v = 5091.75 m/s, f = 2121.56 Hz, and d = 8.08366 cm.
assumptions: The stated thin rod follows the one-dimensional linear elastic longitudinal-wave model.
The light disc negligibly loads the rod.
For the current-run extensions, the stated 1.2 m is the length before extension, and the clamp is fitted at the midpoint of the completed rod.
The earlier-run extensions are absent during the stated measurement.

T94AF.regime: Thin-rod longitudinal-wave approximation; all listed diameters satisfy 10q < Lr with lengths expressed in metres.

T9574.regime: Thin-rod longitudinal-wave approximation; all listed diameters satisfy 10q < Lr with lengths expressed in metres.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with d = cL sqrt(rho/Y): extensions of 14, 32 and 55 cm give 9.02676, 10.2393 and 11.7887 cm. Cross-sectional area cancels between axial rigidity YA and linear density rho A. I accept the diameter assignments as K because thinness conditions the applicability of this cancellation; pass 1 classified them as C within the already assumed one-dimensional model. All listed diameters are well inside the stated slenderness regime, whose threshold is an approximation criterion rather than an exact physical transition. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies TFBD6 and TFE55 as deliberately numeral-free controls, rather than numerical minimal pairs. The actual claimed minimal pairs T2604/TD83B and TA297/T3295 preserve the quantity, number and unit while changing its attachment or timing. The cancellation expressions require consistent units, including conversion of Young's modulus from MPa to Pa.
